scenarioResolutionOutcomes._notes: Per-scenario Succeed/Failed (curation judgement). Success = you escaped / met the objective / defeated the threat; loss = defeated or failed the objective. Pure doubt-vs-conviction sub-choices within a success both count as success (e.g. Curtain Call warn/not). Dim Carcosa R2 (you take the stage — possessed) is `win` like R1/R3: all three record `prevented_hasturs_escape` and end on a `win` step in ArkhamCards (R2's text closes with 'The investigators win the campaign!'); only R4 (Carcosa merged) and R5 (Hastur has you) are `loss`. `record_possessed_investigators` fires in all three win endings, so possession marks no distinct outcome. The Last King: survived = win, all-defeated = loss, resigned = neutral (a voluntary early exit).

scenarioMaxXp._notes: Maximum victory-display XP awardable per scenario — the reference 'Max' column. 0 means the victory display awards nothing here (the scenario grants its XP some other way), shown as a dash rather than a number.

vips_interviewed._note: Whitelist the picker to the five VIP guest ASSETS (03076a Constance, 03077 Jordan, 03078 Haruko, 03079 Sebastien, 03080 Ashleigh). ArkhamCards the_last_king records VIPs Interviewed via card_choice query [03076a,03077,03078,03079,03080], and its own branches check vips_interviewed for these asset codes. Extract captured vips_slain's whitelist (the 03065b-03069b ENEMY sides) but not this one. Without it the picker offered the whole card pool incl. the enemy sides.

doubt._note: 7 doubt/conviction sources campaign-wide (Curtain Call, Reality's Shadow [R1 only], Echoes, Lost Soul +2, Phantom, Pallid Mask +2, Black Stars Rise). Single-side max is 8 on a normal path (= the 'win with 8 Doubt' achievement) but 9 if you resigned at The Last King and thus also played Reality's Shadow. Cap at 9 so the resign-path edge isn't blocked.

conviction._note: See doubt: single-side max 8 normal / 9 on the resign->Reality's Shadow path. Cap 9 ('win with 8 Conviction' achievement still triggers at >=8).

sections._chasing_the_stranger_note: chasing_the_stranger is intentionally NOT capped (no override). The Man in the Pallid Mask is DISCARDED (not removed) when defeated, so a deck reshuffle can resurface him for another defeat in the same scenario — the tally is unbounded. Dim Carcosa's 6-8 doom bracket is just where the effect plateaus, not a hard ceiling. This key matches no real section id, so apply.mjs ignores it.

entryOverrides._note: The Pallid Mask resolution records '#name# read Act 2 of The King in Yellow.' PER INVESTIGATOR — every investigator present reads it, so it must be recordable multiple times (once per investigator). The extractor can't infer repeatability from the tree, so mark it repeatable and restrict the #name# card picker to investigators (the default pool is all unique player cards). Same pattern as side.json's Fortune and Folly Stashed/Alarm level.

campaign_notes.possessed._note: Dim Carcosa records the name of each investigator who ended the game possessed (a Possession treachery in hand). The source captures names via investigator_choice but extract flattened it to a presence-only note — so mark it repeatable (one entry per possessed investigator) and restrict the #name# picker to investigators (NotesSection then scopes it to the party). The WHO now rides the log: life reads the repeated picks as possessedInvestigators, so the old Extra possessed_investigators picker is dropped.

the_pallid_mask.label: Random basic weakness added (read Act 2)
the_pallid_mask._note: Pallid Mask: each investigator who read Act II of The King in Yellow searches the collection for a random basic Madness or Pact weakness and adds it to their deck (and earns 2 XP). A card draw, not logged -> Extra. Filtered card picker (subtype basicweakness + Madness/Pact traits); multiple picks join with commas. Mirrors black_stars_rise.randomized_weakness but narrower (BSR allows Cultist/Detective too). WHO read Act II is the repeatable read_act_2 campaign-log entry; this records the weakness each drew. Slotted after the resolution but BEFORE slew_vip + the victory display (the Act II read is a mid-scenario card draw).

the_pallid_mask.label: Investigator who drew each (same order as above)
the_pallid_mask._note: Pairs BY INDEX with randomized_weakness: the investigator who drew each random weakness, listed in the same order (each investigator who read Act II draws one). Investigator card picker, mirrors insane_investigators; multi-pick comma-joined. ptc.ts zips the two lists to attribute each weakness to its bearer and groups by (weakness, bearer). Optional — when empty the weakness still shows, just without a bearer. Folded into randomized_weakness's per-investigator field (never a standalone field), so its own slot is moot.

black_stars_rise._note: BSR's Blue Star's Demise agenda marks +1 Conviction (doom on agenda 1a <=2) or +1 Doubt (>=3), and neither if 1a wasn't the current agenda — board state, not logged -> Extra. Radio auto-prepends a '—' (blank) option, which stands in for the neither/not-applicable case, so only Conviction/Doubt are explicit choices. buildDcRun ignores anything that isn't 'conviction'/'doubt'.

outcomes._notes: Auto-proposed by tools/outcomes.mjs, then CORRECTED: dropped campaign_notes.possessed from win. Dim Carcosa has exactly ONE winning log — prevented_hasturs_escape. `possessed` is NOT a win/loss ending; it merely flags that investigators ended possessed, which makes the Epilogue occur (and co-occurs with the win resolutions R1-R3). Listing it as a win made a bogus 'someone was possessed.' ending appear in the coverage passport. If outcomes.mjs is re-run it will re-propose it — keep it out. (R4 carcosa_merged / R5 hastur_has_you are the genuine losses.)
